Below is a plan for a software change. Decide, for each reference problem, whether the plan addresses the same underlying problem anywhere in its text (names it as a risk, or plans for it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Allow an article to have several co-authors, while keeping existing article URLs and API responses working for current clients.

Reference problems:
1. In src/app/routes/article/article.mapper.ts, articleMapper explicitly formats author: authorMapper(article.author, id). If this is replaced with an authors array rather than retaining the singular author field, existing Conduit API clients expecting a single author object will break.
2. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, updateArticle generates newSlug as ${slugify(article.title)}-${id} using the authenticated user's ID. If a co-author edits the title, the slug will incorporate the co-author's ID instead of the original author's ID, mutating the slug and breaking existing article URLs.
3. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, updateArticle and deleteArticle enforce permissions via existingArticle.author.id !== id. Without careful refactoring, this logic will either reject legitimate co-authors with a 403 Forbidden error on updates or naively allow any co-author to permanently delete an article without the primary author's consent.
4. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, buildFindAllQuery filters by author using author: { AND: [{ username: { equals: query.author } }] }. If the underlying Prisma model transitions to multiple authors without updating this filter to inspect relation lists (e.g., authors: { some: ... }), querying GET /articles?author=:username will fail at runtime or omit co-authored articles.
5. In src/prisma/schema.prisma, Article currently defines a scalar authorId Int foreign key referencing User. Replacing authorId with a many-to-many relation without a careful migration script to backfill existing records into the new join table will corrupt foreign keys or cause permanent loss of existing authorship data.
6. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, getFeed fetches articles matching author: { followedBy: { some: { id } } }. If this query is expanded to check multiple authors without applying distinct selection, users who follow more than one co-author of the same article will receive duplicate articles and corrupted pagination counts.
7. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, favoriteArticle and unfavoriteArticle build response payloads directly using profileMapper(article.author, id) rather than articleMapper. Updating the Prisma include statements and response models only in articleMapper will cause runtime crashes during favorite/unfavorite operations due to referencing undefined article.author.
8. In src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, createArticle only connects a single author via the authenticated user's ID. Introducing co-authors in the creation payload without validating user existence, preventing duplicate IDs, or establishing an authorization/invitation mechanism could allow arbitrary author impersonation or unhandled database constraint exceptions.

Plan:
# Co-authors for articles: [term] plan ([term] `--standard`, stopped after [term])

I didn't edit any repo files. The plan is saved at `claude-home/plans/standard-allow-an-article-breezy-sundae.md`. The entry check passed. The repo is small, so I read the code myself instead of sending out research subagents. I skipped web research because a join table is the well-known pattern here. The repo has no record of past project lessons to consult.

## Assumptions (stated instead of asking)
- **The current `author` stays the owner.** In responses it stays a single profile object. Co-authors are extra users on top of it.
- **One new response field.** Article responses gain `coAuthors: Profile[]`, always present, `[]` by default and kept in a fixed order.
- **Input:** `article.coAuthors` is optional on POST and PUT.
  - If the key is missing on PUT, the list stays as it is.
  - Items can be usernames or `{username}` objects.
- **Permissions:**
  - Only the owner can change the co-author list or delete the article.
  - Co-authors can edit title, description, body and tags.
- **List endpoints don't change.** `?author=` and `/articles/feed` still match only the owner, so counts don't move for current clients. A new optional `?contributor=` filter matches the owner or a co-author.
- **URLs don't change.** The slug format `slugify(title)-<ownerId>` stays, and adding co-authors never changes a slug. Renaming the slug when the title changes already happens today and is out of scope.

## Main facts from the code
- **Slug bug that co-authors would expose:** `updateArticle` builds the new slug from the **caller's** id (`src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts:317`). That only works because today the caller is always the author. If a co-author renamed an article, its URL would end in their id.
- **Favorite responses leak data:** `favoriteArticle` and `unfavoriteArticle` return the raw database row (`article.service.ts:597-603`). That row includes `favoritedBy` user rows with password hashes. This leak already exists.
- **Repeated query block:** the same `include` block appears 7 times. Article visibility ("author is a demo user or me") is decided at `article.service.ts:8-67` and repeated in `tag.service.ts`.

## Plan
| ID | What changes | How it's checked |
|---|---|---|
| D01 | New `ArticleCoAuthor` table (article, user, position, created date; keyed on article + user; deleting either side deletes the row). The `Article` table is untouched and no data needs filling in. | `prisma migrate diff --from-schema-datamodel … --script` shows only new table, index and foreign-key statements (no database needed) |
| D02 | One shared `articleInclude` that selects only username, bio, image and followers for co-authors. `articleMapper` adds `coAuthors` and treats a missing value as `[]`. | Existing response keys unchanged plus `coAuthors`; tests check the arguments passed to the mocked database, not just the returned data |
| D03 | Write path: check co-author usernames (unknown, duplicates, the owner listed again, more than 10 → 422). Edit rights are owner or co-author; changing the list or deleting is owner only. Slug built from `authorId`. List replaced inside the same database update. | Tests for owner, co-author and a stranger. A co-author renames the article and the slug keeps the owner's id. A client sends a GET response back unchanged as a PUT and gets 200. |
| D04 | Read path: articles are also visible to their co-authors; new `?contributor=` filter. `buildFindAllQuery` exported so it can be tested. | Tests on the generated query; the `?author=` query is identical to today's |
| D05 | Tests and docs | `nx test` and `nx lint` pass; README documents the new field and filter, and that the feed doesn't include co-authored articles |

## [term] result
An independent subagent saw only the plan and returned **REVISE** with 3 high-severity issues. All of them are fixed in revision 1:
- **Clients that send articles back would break.** Many Conduit clients PUT back the article they got from GET, which would now include `coAuthors`. Those edits would fail with 422 or 403. Fix: accept both input shapes, and treat an unchanged list as no change.
- **The favorite-endpoint leak contradicted the no-password test.** The leak is now recorded as an accepted, existing issue for a follow-up, so the test is scoped to `coAuthors` and the endpoints that use the mapper.
- **Mock-based tests can't catch a wrong database select**, because the mock returns whatever it's given. Fix: assert on the arguments passed to the mock instead.

It also flagged two medium points, now recorded as risks:
- **Consent:** an owner can name any user as a co-author.
- **Tags get wiped:** a PUT without `tagList` clears the tags. This already happens today, and co-authors now inherit it.

Standard mode allows one [term] round, so revision 1 has not been re-[term].

## Main risks

| # | Risk | Why it bites here | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clients that send articles back break | Many Conduit clients PUT back the GET body, which will now include `coAuthors` | Accept both input shapes; unchanged list = no change; test sending GET back as PUT |
| 2 | Co-author edit changes the URL | Slug is built from the caller's id (`:317`) | Build it from `authorId`; test |
| 3 | Password hashes leak through co-authors | Favorite endpoints return the raw row | Select only profile fields; map co-authors through `profileMapper` |
| 4 | Permissions too wide or too narrow | Every check today compares only `author.id` | `canEdit`/`isOwner` helpers; test each role |
| 5 | Article counts change for current clients | `?author=` and feed counts would include co-authored articles | Keep owner-only meaning; new `?contributor=` |
| 6 | Tests pass but real queries are wrong | Database is fully mocked | Assert on query arguments and the shared include |
| 7 | Migration isn't purely additive | It runs automatically at container start | Only creates a table; diff checked without a database; old code ignores the table |
| 8 | Partial co-author list after an error | Remove and re-add done as separate steps | Do both inside one `update` |
| 9 | Users named as co-authors without consent | Owner can add anyone | Accepted and documented; self-removal endpoint as follow-up |
| 10 | Co-author edit wipes tags | A PUT without `tagList` clears tags (`:335-343`) | Already happens today; documented, not changed |

Riskiest: #1, current clients sending the GET response back as a PUT. Once `coAuthors` appears in responses, those clients' content edits would fail unless the API ignores an unchanged co-author list.
